description.summary: which window is where, and a picture of one, for one trusted client

protocol.description:
A compositor tells no ordinary client where windows are or what they show. This protocol lets one trusted client ask, one window at a time: which window is at a point, which window has focus, and a picture of a window it was just told about. It exists so a person can point at a window (drag a mark onto it, or press a key while it has focus) and ask about that window.
The compositor offers this global only to the client it launched itself as the locator. It sends nothing unasked: every event answers a request, so the client never learns about a window it did not ask about. Nothing is answered while the session is locked.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made.

interface.name: zyantrik_window_locator_v1

description.summary: the window locator, for the client labwc launched

interface.description:
at and focused each take a serial chosen by the client and are answered by exactly one window or none event carrying that serial, in the order they were made. capture is answered by exactly one picture or capture_failed event naming the same window.
A picture may be taken only of the window named by the most recent answer to at or focused, only while that answer is at most two seconds old, and only once per answer: a none answer, a later window answer or a capture request each use it up, except a capture refused as not_located or throttled. That is how the client is held to the person's gesture: it locates the window under the person's pointer or focus, then captures it.
Window ids are stable while the window exists. An id is given to a window the first time an answer names it, and is not given to another window until 2^32 more have been named.

entry.name: nothing
entry.summary: no window there, or something that is not a window (a panel, a dock, a menu) is on top there

entry.name: throttled
entry.summary: more than 120 at and focused requests in the last second

entry.name: not_located
entry.summary: not the window of the most recent answer, that answer is over two seconds old, or it was already used

entry.name: gone
entry.summary: the window closed or was unmapped

entry.name: throttled
entry.summary: more than 2 pictures in the last second

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: the compositor could not draw the picture

request.name: at

description.summary: which window is at this point

request.description: The topmost window at x, y in layout coordinates, counting its decorations and popups. The client's own surfaces are looked through, so a full-screen overlay it draws during a drag does not hide what is under it. Anything else on top at that point (another client's panel, dock or popup, a menu, the lock screen) answers none with reason nothing.

request.name: focused
request.description: The window that has keyboard focus, or none with reason nothing.

request.name: capture

description.summary: a picture of the window just located

request.description: A picture of the window's own content, rendered from that window alone: never its decorations and never anything overlapping it. It fits max_width x max_height, each first held to 16..2048, and is never larger than the window. See the interface description for which window may be captured, and when.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the window, as the most recent answer named it

event.name: window

description.summary: the window there, or the focused window

event.description: app_id and title are each cut to 511 bytes. x, y, width and height are the window's content in layout coordinates, without decorations.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: app id (Wayland) or class (X11); empty if none

event.name: picture
event.description: Premultiplied ARGB8888 (DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888, little-endian), height rows of stride bytes, in a sealed memory file the client maps read only and closes.
